# Function to check if a port responds

    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Try to connect to the port with a short timeout using curl
    if timeout 5 bash -c "</dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✅ $service_name (port $port): UP"
        return 0
    else
        echo "❌ $service_name (port $port): DOWN"
        return 1
    fi

    echo "Loading environment variables from .env.test..."
    export $(grep -v '^#' .env.test | xargs)

    echo "Warning: .env.test file not found"

frontend_status=$?

    overall_status="healthy"
    echo -e "\n🎉 All services are running!"

    overall_status="degraded"
    echo -e "\n⚠️  Some services are down!"
fi

# Send health report to monitoring dashboard
echo "Sending health report to monitoring dashboard..."

# Create JSON payload with health status and credentials

  "status": "$overall_status",
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)",
  "services": {
    "frontend": {
      "port": 3000,
      "status": "$([ $frontend_status -eq 0 ] && echo "up" || echo "down")"

    "backend": {
      "port": 8080,

  }
}
EOF
)

  -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$payload" \
  http://localhost:47301/api/health-report)

if [ "$response" -eq 200 ]; then
    echo "✅ Health report sent successfully to monitoring dashboard"
else
    echo "❌ Failed to send health report (HTTP $response)"
fi

# Exit with appropriate code based on service status
if [ "$overall_status" = "healthy" ]; then
    exit 0
else
    exit 1
fi
